page: Vultr voc-g-96c-256gb-1280s-amd is an Optimized Cloud Compute server instance configured with 96 dedicated vCPUs mapped from 48 physical AMD EPYC cores. Operating at a clock speed of 2.0 GHz on the x86_64 architecture, this server features 256.0 GB of system memory, yielding a memory-to-core ratio of 2.67 GB per vCPU. Local storage is provided by a bundled 1280 GB NVMe SSD, and the instance includes one complimentary public IPv4 address. No dedicated GPU hardware is present on this configuration.

Benchmark evaluations indicate strong multi-core processing capabilities, with stress-ng multi-core performance ranking in the top 10% at 213,580.47. PassMark CPU extended instructions and encryption tests also place in the top 10%, reflecting robust cryptographic and vector execution. Cached small-block memory read bandwidth is highly efficient at 8,120.31 GB/sec, though large-block uncached read and write memory bandwidths align with average tier performance at 145.72 GB/sec and 72.97 GB/sec respectively. Single-threaded operations present a relative bottleneck, as demonstrated by a weak rating in gzip compression and average single-core Geekbench scores.

From a resource density perspective, this server offers high compute density with dedicated AMD EPYC cores, making it a qualitatively cost-efficient option for highly parallelized workloads that do not require massive memory footprints per thread. The high multi-threaded performance and strong multi-threaded bzip3 decompression throughput make this instance suitable for software compilation, ray tracing, and multi-threaded data processing. It is also well-suited for high-throughput Redis operations, static web serving, and moderate-scale LLM inference tasks.

This hardware profile is highly suited for multi-threaded software compilation, ray tracing, high-throughput Redis deployments, and moderate LLM inference workloads.
